title: Thanthai Periyar and the Press Conference: 'Attack My Person, But You Cannot Disprove Reason'
summary: Facing hostile questions from orthodox journalists, Thanthai Periyar demonstrated serene patience, declaring that personal attacks could never extinguish rationalist truth.
full_text:
In the early 1960s, inside a press room in Chennai, eighty-something-year-old Periyar E. V. Ramasamy sat before a phalanx of political correspondents.

A reporter representing an orthodox daily sought to provoke the veteran social reformer:
"Mr. Ramasamy, you have spent decades preaching atheism and attacking caste orthodoxy. People throw stones, footwear, and rotten vegetables at your public meetings! Does it not humiliate you to face such public scorn? Why do you not retire in peace instead of courting contempt?"

Periyar's young aides bristled with anger, but Periyar raised his hand with an affectionate smile, thoroughly enjoying the exchange:
"My dear friend, why should that humiliate me? In fact, I regard those flying slippers as the highest involuntary tribute to the power of our ideas!
When people resort to throwing stones and mud at a speaker, it is proof positive that they have run out of logical arguments! It is the desperate weapon of an ideological monopoly that has no answers to reason.

You may revile my person, you may slander my name, and you may even extinguish this frail, aging body. But the principles I advocate—human equality, self-respect, gender emancipation, and scientific rationalism—are immortal! You cannot shoot an idea with a bullet, nor can you bury reason in a grave. One day, our youth will awaken to critical thought, and on that day, our words will prevail!"

The room fell into respectful silence. Periyar’s indomitable courage turned personal vilification into a badge of unshakeable conviction.
